text: 68-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes came for her routine diabetes follow-up but the nurse sent her to the ED. She says she is just tired and slightly nauseated since this morning, and has an ache in her jaw she blames on a dental filling last week. No chest pain. HR 102, BP 138/84, RR 18, SpO2 96%.

23-year-old man brought by his flatmate. After an argument 5 hours ago he swallowed 'a handful' of paracetamol tablets. He now feels completely fine, is calm and polite, apologises for wasting time and asks to go home. HR 76, BP 122/70, RR 14, SpO2 99%.

35-year-old woman with known asthma, wheezy for 2 days, used her blue inhaler many times. Now drowsy, can only say one or two words, and the triage nurse hears very little wheeze on auscultation. HR 130, RR 10, SpO2 91% on room air.

40-year-old man with 3 years of chronic low back pain, asks for a stronger painkiller because 'it is the usual pain'. When asked, he mentions numbness around his buttocks and groin since yesterday and that he has had difficulty starting to pass urine. Vitals normal, pain 6/10.

70-year-old man, day 10 after his latest cycle of chemotherapy for lymphoma, says he feels 'basically OK' but his wife insisted he come because he felt shivery. Temp 38.1, HR 96, BP 118/70, RR 18, SpO2 97%.

30-year-old woman, 34 weeks pregnant with her first baby, has a headache she thinks is from poor sleep and says she keeps seeing sparkly lights. Mild swelling of hands and face. BP 162/108, HR 90, SpO2 99%.

45-year-old man fell onto his outstretched hand while cycling 3 hours ago. Tender in the anatomical snuffbox, no deformity, fingers warm with normal sensation. Needs a wrist X-ray and will probably need a splint. HR 80, BP 130/82, pain 4/10.

19-year-old woman with a sore throat and fever for 1 day, asking for throat lozenges. Her medication list shows carbimazole started 3 weeks ago for Graves disease. Temp 38.3, HR 108, BP 112/70, SpO2 98%.

58-year-old man, smoker, has had 'indigestion' in the centre of his chest for 2 weeks that comes on when walking to the station and goes within minutes of stopping. This morning it came on while sitting watching TV and lasted 20 minutes. Now pain free, looks well, wants an appointment next week.

34-year-old woman with years of brief self-terminating episodes of palpitations, none in the past month. Feels well today, no syncope, no chest pain. ECG in clinic today: sinus rhythm 72, short PR interval with a delta wave. Vitals normal.

62-year-old man noticed yellow eyes and dark urine over 3 weeks, itchy skin, and has lost 6 kg without trying. No pain, no fever, no rigors, eating and drinking, fully alert. HR 78, BP 132/80, Temp 36.8.

25-year-old man woke from sleep 3 hours ago with sudden pain in his left testicle and vomited once. He says it is 'a bit better now' and wonders if it is a pulled muscle from the gym. The left testis sits slightly higher than the right.

71-year-old man with hypertension says that yesterday he lost vision in his right eye 'like a curtain coming down' for about 5 minutes, then it fully returned. He feels normal now and his eye examination today is normal.

45-year-old woman with known hypertension who stopped her amlodipine a month ago. BP 184/112 on repeated clinic readings. Completely asymptomatic: no headache, chest pain, breathlessness, visual change, or neurological symptoms. Fundoscopy normal, urine dipstick normal, recent creatinine normal.

30-year-old woman with fever 38.4, headache and muscle aches for 2 days, thinks it is flu. She returned 10 days ago from visiting family in Ghana and did not take antimalarial tablets. Otherwise alert and drinking well.

55-year-old man with bipolar disorder, stable for years on lithium, has had vomiting and diarrhoea for 2 days. Today his family noticed a coarse tremor of his hands, he is unsteady on his feet and his speech is slightly slurred.

50-year-old man with fatigue, pain in the 2nd and 3rd knuckles of both hands, newly diagnosed diabetes, and skin that looks tanned in winter. Ferritin 1800 ug/L, transferrin saturation 70%, ALT mildly raised. HFE C282Y homozygous.

29-year-old woman with repeated sudden episodes of racing heart, chest tightness, tingling fingers and a feeling she is about to die, peaking within 10 minutes. She now avoids public transport. ECG, 7-day Holter, echocardiogram and thyroid function are all normal.

45-year-old man with episodes of pounding headache, sweating and palpitations, and blood pressure that swings up to 220/120 during attacks despite three antihypertensives. Plasma free metanephrines are four times the upper limit of normal.
60-year-old woman with gritty dry eyes, a dry mouth needing water to swallow food, and swelling of both parotid glands. Anti-Ro antibody positive, Schirmer test abnormal.

66-year-old man referred with low mood. His wife says his handwriting has become small, he is slow to get going, he shuffles when he walks and his right hand shakes when resting on his lap, less when he reaches for a cup.
48-year-old woman with generalised itching but no rash, and marked tiredness. Alkaline phosphatase 3 times normal, bilirubin normal, anti-mitochondrial antibody positive.
Patient: 82-year-old woman, weight 52 kg, serum creatinine 160 umol/L, newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation. Prescription: dabigatran 150 mg twice daily.

Patient: 70-year-old man, weight 80 kg, serum creatinine 90 umol/L, confirmed proximal DVT, no bleeding history. Prescription: enoxaparin 80 mg subcutaneously twice daily as bridge to oral anticoagulation.
Patient: 55-year-old man on methadone 120 mg daily for opioid dependence, recent ECG QTc 490 ms, has a chest infection. Prescription: azithromycin 500 mg daily for 3 days.

Patient: 30-year-old woman, non-smoker, BMI 23, migraine with visual aura twice a month, requests contraception. Prescription: combined oral contraceptive pill (ethinylestradiol 30 mcg / levonorgestrel 150 mcg).
Patient: 72-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and heart failure with ejection fraction 30%, NYHA class III, HbA1c 8.4% on metformin. Prescription: add pioglitazone 30 mg daily.
Patient: 45-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease, eGFR 35, potassium 5.6 mmol/L this week, on ramipril 10 mg daily, has resistant hypertension. Prescription: add spironolactone 25 mg daily.
Patient: 8-year-old child, weight 25 kg, sprained ankle, no asthma, no kidney disease, eating normally. Prescription: ibuprofen 250 mg three times daily with food for 3 days.
Patient: 3-year-old child, weight 14 kg, after tonsillectomy for obstructive sleep apnoea. Prescription: codeine 1 mg/kg every 6 hours as needed for pain.
Patient: 50-year-old man with Crohn's disease maintained on azathioprine 150 mg daily, now has recurrent gout. Prescription: allopurinol 300 mg daily.

Patient: 66-year-old woman on levothyroxine 100 mcg each morning, osteopenia. Prescription: calcium carbonate 1.25 g with vitamin D daily, with written advice to take it at least 4 hours after the levothyroxine.

Patient: 32-year-old woman, 20 weeks pregnant, symptomatic lower urinary tract infection, normal kidney function, no G6PD deficiency. Prescription: nitrofurantoin modified-release 100 mg twice daily for 7 days.

Patient: 58-year-old man on atorvastatin 40 mg daily and amlodipine 5 mg, community-acquired chest infection, normal ECG, no penicillin allergy but amoxicillin failed. Prescription: azithromycin 500 mg daily for 3 days.

45-year-old man, heavy drinker, stopped drinking 2 days ago because of vomiting and has barely eaten. Abdominal pain. No history of diabetes. Glucose 6.1 mmol/L, pH 7.25, bicarbonate 12, Na 135, Cl 98, lactate 1.5, serum osmolal gap normal, urine ketones 3+.

32-year-old woman, 5 days after a vaginal delivery with an epidural. Worsening headache for 2 days, now worse when lying down and in the morning, vomiting, and she had a seizure this morning. BP 128/80, urine protein negative, bilateral papilloedema.

70-year-old male smoker with his first ever episode of severe left flank pain radiating to the groin, started suddenly an hour ago. Urine dipstick shows blood. He looks pale and sweaty. BP 90/60, HR 115.

24-year-old woman had a bout of diarrhoea 2 weeks ago. For 3 days she has had tingling feet and weakness climbing stairs that now involves her hands. Knee and ankle reflexes absent. Potassium 3.9 mmol/L. No eye or bladder symptoms.

55-year-old woman treated for breast cancer 3 years ago, brought in with a week of new confusion, constipation, passing large volumes of urine, thirst and bone aches. No focal neurological signs, no fever.

65-year-old man with COPD, more breathless over 2 days with right-sided pleuritic chest pain and temperature 37.8. Flew back from Australia 5 days ago; right calf swollen. Chest X-ray clear, no increase in sputum. SpO2 90%, HR 112.
35-year-old woman with months of tiredness, weight loss, craving salt, and dizziness on standing. Skin creases and gums look darker. Na 124, K 5.9, glucose 3.6 mmol/L, BP 90/60. Takes no medication.
40-year-old woman with known gallstones: 2 days of right upper quadrant pain, rigors, yellow eyes, now confused. Temp 39.2, BP 84/50. Lipase normal.

45-year-old woman on sertraline 150 mg daily was started on tramadol 2 days ago for back pain. Now agitated, sweating, diarrhoea, temperature 38.7, HR 124, brisk reflexes and sustained clonus at both ankles. Muscles not rigid.

38-year-old man with diabetes, sharp central chest pain for a day that is worse lying back and eased by sitting forward. Had flu last week. ECG: widespread concave ST elevation in most leads with PR depression, no reciprocal changes. Troponin normal. Blood pressure equal in both arms.

56-year-old man with 45 minutes of crushing chest pain. ECG: 3 mm ST elevation in V1-V4. A primary PCI centre can take him with an expected door-to-balloon time of 60 minutes. No contraindications to any treatment.

options.D: Repeat troponin at 3 hours then decide

text: 74-year-old woman on warfarin for atrial fibrillation, routine INR 8.5 after a course of antibiotics. No bleeding of any kind, haemoglobin stable, no recent falls.

options.A: Continue warfarin at the same dose and recheck in a week
options.B: Withhold warfarin and give oral vitamin K

text: 66-year-old man with chronic kidney disease, potassium 7.1 mmol/L. ECG shows tall peaked T waves and broadened QRS complexes. He is alert and haemodynamically stable.

25-year-old woman with 6 weeks of amenorrhoea, lower abdominal pain and shoulder-tip pain. Urine hCG positive. Transvaginal ultrasound: empty uterus, large volume of free fluid. BP 82/50, HR 128 despite 1 litre of fluid.
22-year-old man with type 1 diabetes: glucose 28 mmol/L, pH 7.10, bicarbonate 8, ketones 5.8, potassium 3.0 mmol/L. He has had 1 litre of 0.9% saline.

options.B: Replace potassium and delay insulin until potassium is at least 3.3

text: 19-year-old student in the ED with fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and photophobia for 12 hours. GCS 14, no papilloedema, no focal neurological signs, no seizures. CT scanner has a 90-minute wait.

options.A: CT head first, then lumbar puncture, then antibiotics
options.C: Take blood cultures and give IV ceftriaxone now
options.D: Oral amoxicillin and review in the morning

text: 72-year-old man with right-sided weakness and aphasia that began 2 hours ago. CT head: no haemorrhage. NIHSS 8. BP 200/115, glucose 7. No other contraindication to thrombolysis.

options.B: Lower BP below 185/110, then give IV thrombolysis
options.C: Aspirin 300 mg and admit to the stroke unit
options.D: Withhold thrombolysis because of the blood pressure

text: 29-year-old woman, 36 weeks pregnant, BP 170/112, 3+ proteinuria, severe frontal headache and brisk reflexes with 3 beats of clonus.

options.A: Oral amlodipine and review in antenatal clinic in 3 days
options.B: IV magnesium sulfate and IV antihypertensive, plan delivery
options.C: Bed rest and repeat BP in 4 hours
